The interviews in question, known as the "Boston Tapes," are part of the Belfast Project, an oral history initiative conducted from 2001 to 2006, where dozens of former paramilitaries were interviewed in Belfast and other locations.

Ben Davies, the 21-year-old Welsh defender, is moving to the London club on a five-year contract, while 30-year-old Dutch goalkeeper Michel Vorm has committed to a four-year deal. Meanwhile, Gylfi Sigurdsson, the 24-year-old Icelandic midfielder, returns to Swansea on a four-year contract, having previously played for them on loan from Hoffenheim in 2011-12, where he scored seven goals in 18 games. Tottenham reportedly faced strong competition for Davies, with Liverpool's manager Brendan Rodgers among those interested. Davies stated that Tottenham's pursuit was consistent from the start, making the opportunity "too good an opportunity to turn down". He mentioned on Swansea's website that he never intended to leave, but an opportunity like this was too good to pass up.

According to Jiangsu's pricing regulator, Mercedes-Benz, the German luxury car manufacturer, coerced its local dealerships to enforce minimum sales prices on specific car models, resulting in fines of 7.7 million yuan for some dealers. A Mercedes-Benz representative stated that the company acknowledges the ruling and is committed to adhering to competition law, adding that they have taken necessary actions to ensure full legal compliance. The Chinese regulator's statement revealed that Mercedes-Benz and its Jiangsu dealers were found to have engaged in monopolistic practices by setting minimum sales prices for E-Class and S-Class models, as well as certain spare parts. In the previous year, Xinhua reported that Mercedes-Benz was also found guilty of manipulating after-sales service prices in China, which is the world's largest car market for foreign automakers.

S4C primarily relies on the licence fee for funding, and with the UK government initiating a significant review of the BBC, the future of S4C is under discussion. David Davies, MP for Monmouth, emphasized to BBC Wales that S4C is a "special case" due to its role in promoting the Welsh language. Despite this, ministers have suggested S4C should strive for cost reductions similar to those at the BBC. Labour party expressed concerns on Thursday that budget cuts to the BBC could endanger S4C. However, Culture Secretary John Whittingdale assured MPs of a commitment to the channel "within the next couple of years" and expressed his intention to engage in discussions with S4C's management soon. Speaking on BBC Radio Cymru's Rhaglen Dylan Jones on Friday, Mr. Davies stated, "The government realize the importance of S4C and that it's more than a station, it's important to the future of the Welsh language." He also suggested that the Welsh Affairs Committee, which he leads, might investigate broadcasting matters, including S4C.

In August 1974, a body was discovered in Cockley Cley, near Swaffham, Norfolk. Norfolk Police are now employing advanced methods for a second post-mortem examination. Det Ch Insp Andy Guy stated the recovered DNA could potentially connect the woman to a living relative. The initial post-mortem, conducted on the day of the body's discovery on a heath, estimated her age to be between 23 and 35. She was found wearing a 1969 Marks & Spencer pink nightdress, wrapped in a plastic sheet tied with ropes. Investigators are primarily focusing on the possibility that she was "The Duchess," an escort from Great Yarmouth. Detectives believe The Duchess, who was well-known in the area and thought to be from Denmark, vanished unexpectedly.

This research examined men in demanding army cadet training against a control group to see if environmental changes impacted their preferences for female body types. The study revealed that men in training showed a greater attraction to women with heavier builds. Dr. Carlota Batres, the lead researcher, suggested this shift might be an adaptation to prioritize partners who are more likely to thrive and reproduce in challenging conditions. She emphasized that the study highlights how adaptable mate preferences can be based on environmental factors, noting that preferences shifted and remained altered as long as the harsh environment persisted. According to Dr. Batres, these changes could be advantageous, increasing the likelihood of forming relationships with individuals better suited to withstand illness or food scarcity. Foreign Affairs Secretary Perfecto Yasay plans to address the South China Sea issue at the upcoming Asia-Europe summit, a two-day event beginning Friday and attended by Chinese Premier Li Keqiang. This summit follows a UN tribunal's decision on Tuesday invalidating China's claims in the region, a ruling China has rejected, asserting the tribunal's lack of jurisdiction and affirming its continued activities there. The Asia-Europe Meeting Summit (Asem) in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, marks the first significant multilateral diplomatic forum since the July 12 ruling. The summit will host 53 leaders from Asia and Europe, including representatives from Vietnam and Malaysia, both of which have territorial claims in the South China Sea. It also represents the inaugural meeting for the new Philippine government.

After colliding with a car on the A9 while driving an articulated lorry, John McCormack continued driving for 30 miles. Perth Sheriff Court heard that the car contained three children during the incident. McCormack, 46, received a sentence of 250 hours of unpaid work and a two-year driving ban. According to Prosecutor Rebecca Kynaston, drivers traveling north near the House of Bruar shopping center witnessed McCormack's lorry heading directly towards them on the wrong side of the road. She stated that these drivers were able to avoid a collision by moving onto the verge. However, the lorry continued and struck the offside of a car carrying a couple and their three children, scraping along its side.

Kim Little of Seattle Reign won the BBC World Service award, topping a fan poll to become the second recipient. She surpassed Gaelle Enganamouit (FC Rosengard), Amandine Henry (Olympique Lyonnais), Carli Lloyd (Houston Dash), and Becky Sauerbrunn (FC Kansas City). The 25-year-old Little expressed her surprise and humility upon winning, adding her hope for the continued progress of women's football. She received the award at her club's training ground on Tuesday. Mary Hockaday, Controller of BBC World Service English, congratulated Little, highlighting her talent and the remarkable year for women's football. Hockaday also emphasized the BBC World Service's role in recognizing female footballers. Little was Seattle's leading.

Stafford Hospital was allegedly the site of significant neglect, with reports of patients resorting to drinking water from flower vases and unqualified receptionists triaging emergency patients. Julie Bailey, founder of Cure the NHS after her mother's experience, received a CBE for her advocacy. Helene Donnelly, an A&E nurse who exposed the issues, was awarded an OBE. Statistical data indicated a higher-than-expected mortality rate at the hospital between 2005 and 2008. Patients in pain often experienced delays or were denied pain relief altogether, and some were unable to reach food and beverages. Donnelly, who filed almost 100 complaints and testified at the public inquiry, expressed immense pride and honor upon receiving her OBE for her contributions to the NHS, acknowledging the challenges she had faced.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) discovered that credit card companies had little motivation to help customers struggling with persistent debt because these customers generated profit. The FCA advocated for encouraging customers to increase their debt repayments whenever possible. This investigation involved analyzing five years' worth of data from 34 million cardholders and conducting interviews with 40,000 individuals. The FCA's initial findings revealed that while some customers and products faced strong competition, others did not receive targeted offers. Credit card companies promptly assisted customers who missed payments due to their "extreme unprofitability," but this proactive approach was absent for those barely managing to make minimum payments. Joanna Elson, head of the Money Advice Trust, which operates National Debtline, agreed with the FCA's concern for the 1.6 million individuals struggling to stay afloat by making minimum payments, often across multiple credit cards, highlighting that credit card companies typically intervene effectively to support customers.

According to Alex Brazier, the Bank of England's financial stability director, outstanding car loans, credit card balance transfers, and personal loans have surged by 10% in the last year, while household incomes have only grown by 1.5%. Brazier cautioned that "household debt...can be dangerous in excess." In a speech at the University of Liverpool's Institute for Risk and Uncertainty, he stressed that this escalating debt poses a threat to borrowers, lenders, and the broader economy. He also cautioned that High Street banks are vulnerable to "a spiral of complacency" regarding rising consumer debt, noting that "lending standards can go from responsible to reckless very quickly." Bangor University's David Dallimore, a childcare and early years specialist, is advocating for a significant reform of educational services for three- and four-year-olds. Speaking on BBC's Eye on Wales, he stated that Wales has lacked a consistent, long-range plan for early years services. The Welsh government responded that it will evaluate potential changes after reviewing the specifics of the forthcoming Childcare Bill. Currently, all children in this age group are guaranteed at least 10 hours of education through the Foundation Phase. However, each of Wales' 22 local authorities independently decides how to allocate these hours for three-year-olds and determine the funding levels. This decentralization has resulted in substantial disparities in the quality and adaptability of services across different regions, creating an inconsistent and fragmented system.

Taking out the engines, unused for two years, would bring the number of operational vehicles in London to 142. The money saved would be used to hire more firefighters for Fire Rescue Units. However, the Fire Brigades Union (FBU) argues that permanently eliminating these engines would be "dangerous and reckless." The London Fire Brigade (LFB) has presented three cost-cutting plans, emphasizing that no fire stations will be shut down and no firefighters will be laid off. The LFB claims it has consistently met city-wide response time goals even with the 13 engines out of commission, adding that reinstating them would only improve the arrival time of the first engine by roughly four seconds. London Assembly Member Andrew Dismore has suggested a different approach.

Dee Stitt, a prominent UDA figure associated with Charter NI, faced backlash for comments he made to The Guardian. Charter NI's board expressed "deep disappointment and great concern" regarding the article, stating they would handle the issue internally. In the article, Stitt referred to the North Down Defenders loyalist band as "our homeland security" and claimed governmental neglect of Northern Ireland. Charter NI, a community organization, received a Â£1.7m grant from the Northern Ireland Executive's social investment fund. SDLP MLA Nichola Mallon asserted that Stitt's position as CEO of Charter NI was unsustainable and called for his immediate resignation, emphasizing that Charter NI's statement confirmed Stitt's continued role as CEO.

PC Frances Tilley confessed to ruining her career after avoiding paying for a train trip from Bristol Temple Meads to Castle Cary in Somerset last June. During a disciplinary hearing at Northamptonshire Police headquarters, it was revealed she was still on probation, having served less than two years. Consequently, she was fired for gross misconduct. The hearing at Wootton Hall detailed Tilley's journey from Northampton to Castle Cary on June 22nd of the previous year. The officer, who was characterized as "diligent, professional and committed," was traveling with companions and failed to acquire a ticket for the last segment of her trip. Force solicitor Elizabeth Briggs explained that Tilley traveled from Bristol to Westbury and then to Castle Cary without a valid ticket, despite having several chances to buy one.

Reports indicate that a jewelry exhibition at the Carlton Hotel on the Croisette in Cannes was robbed on Sunday morning. This theft is the most significant in a string of notable robberies in Cannes, a city renowned for its film festival. The Carlton Hotel notably served as the filming location for Alfred Hitchcock's "To Catch A Thief," a 1955 film centered on a jewel thief operating on the French Riviera. At the time of the robbery, the hotel lobby was hosting a Leviev diamond exhibition. According to local news outlets, the thief escaped with the jewels in a briefcase, and the owner's identity remains unknown. If the estimated value of the stolen jewels is accurate, this would be the second-largest heist ever in France, according to a Cannes police representative.

Due to ongoing redevelopment at White Hart Lane, Spurs are playing their Champions League home games at Wembley, where they suffered a 1-0 defeat on Wednesday, marking their second European loss at the national stadium this season. Despite this, Pochettino insisted that Wembley is not the issue, stating it's "nowhere better in the world to play football" and placing the blame on the team's performance. With the option to play all home games at Wembley next season, Pochettino expressed embarrassment over their recent performances, particularly the Monaco and Bayer Leverkusen matches, emphasizing the need for internal solutions to their poor showing and expressing disappointment in their inability to replicate their usual form. The Leverkusen loss follows a previous 2-1 defeat at Wembley against Monaco in their Champions League opener.

During a BBC debate at the University of Lincoln concerning the upcoming EU referendum, one panelist described himself as a neutral party "battered on both sides by half-truths, lies and scaremongering." The debate, set to air on Sunday, also featured UKIP MEP Jane Collins (for Leave), Labour MP Melanie Onn (for Remain), and journalist Robin Limb. A key topic of discussion was the NHS's relationship with the EU. Ms. Collins, MEP for Yorkshire and Humber, asserted that the UK contributes £675 million annually to EU health schemes while receiving only £49 million in return, calling it "an atrocity" and advocating for leaving the EU to revitalize the NHS. Ranjit Singh Power, a hotel owner from Wolverhampton, vanished during a business trip to Punjab the previous year. While a taxi driver has admitted to killing him, the BBC's India Correspondent, Sanjoy Majumder, reports that local police suspect he had accomplices. Power's family is seeking the truth about his disappearance and expresses frustration with the lack of information from the Foreign Office and Indian officials. His brother, Amrik Singh Power, stated their ongoing struggle to get answers, emphasizing his continued pleas for information from the Foreign Office. Mr. Power was last seen on May 8th at an airport in Amritsar, Punjab. His family reported him missing after a week of no contact. The taxi driver, Sukhdev Singh, who

In July, the University of Birmingham announced the unearthing of a 1,370-year-old Quran manuscript. University representative Susan Worrall hailed it as "a global treasure." The manuscript is available for public viewing at the Edgbaston campus until October 25, with free admission. The university library stated that the pages of the Islamic holy text had been unnoticed in their collection for nearly a century. A visitor expressed awe, noting the possibility of the Prophet Muhammad or his closest followers having handled the manuscript. Ms. Worrall, the director of special collections, described the discovery as "fantastically exciting," revealing the university possessed one of the world's oldest Quran fragments. Local Muslim leaders in Birmingham have voiced their joy regarding the find. Muhammad Afzal, chairman of Birmingham Central Mosque, shared his sentiments upon seeing the manuscript.

Following Alastair Cook's resignation after a four-year tenure, Yorkshire's Joe Root has been appointed as the new Test captain. Stokes emphasized the team's dual goals of winning and captivating audiences with their performance. Root, 26, previously the vice-captain, will lead England in his first Test match against South Africa at Lord's, starting on July 7th. Durham all-rounder Stokes, 25, will now serve as his deputy. Stokes highlighted the importance of Test cricket, expressing a desire to reignite public passion for the format. Regarding his new role, Stokes affirmed that his focus remains on winning and that the vice-captaincy will not alter his character or playing style, emphasizing his commitment to contributing to all facets of the game.

Addressing soldiers in Siachen, the world's highest battlefield claimed by both India and Pakistan, Prime Minister Modi stated that India enjoys peace of mind due to their constant vigilance. Subsequently, he visited the Kashmir valley, which was devastated by floods that caused at least 281 deaths and submerged Srinagar, displacing over a million people. Modi is the second Indian Prime Minister to visit Siachen, following Manmohan Singh's visit in 2005. Since India gained control in 1984, more soldiers have perished due to the extreme weather conditions on the glacier than in actual combat, with deployments reaching altitudes of 22,000 ft (6,700m). During his visit coinciding with Diwali, the major Hindu festival, Modi met with senior officials and aid workers to assess the ongoing relief efforts. The September floods in Indian-administered Kashmir damaged approximately 180,000 homes, leaving many still residing in relief camps.

The renowned Elephant and Castle nightclub in south-east London has been fighting the construction of an apartment building opposite its location, fearing that noise complaints from future residents might lead to its shutdown. Southwark Council initially denied planning approval, but Boris Johnson has intervened. The Liberal Democrat councillors who rejected the plan faced scrutiny when it was revealed that their party had received significant donations from the club, which they failed to disclose during the meeting. Labour councillors and the developer, Oakmayne, were unaware of the extent of these donations until the BBC revealed them. Furthermore, the council's legal counsel had cautioned the councillors that their failure to declare the donations could be a legal violation. Both Ministry of Sound and the Lib Dems maintain that their actions were entirely legitimate. In a letter to

These revisions would enable Japanese soldiers to engage in combat overseas for the first time since the Second World War. Having already cleared Japan's lower house, the legislation is anticipated to gain approval from the upper chamber. Japan's constitution prohibits the use of force to settle disputes, except in instances of self-defense. However, a new interpretation of the law will now permit "collective self-defense," allowing the use of force to protect allies under attack. Police are present on the streets, directing protesters to move in an effort to reduce disturbances in the capital's core. Despite the rainy conditions, tens of thousands of demonstrators flooded the streets, insisting on the preservation of their pacifist constitution and urging the prime minister's resignation. Although police vans lined the streets, the unprecedented nature of such vocal expression in Japan meant there was little concern of the situation escalating. These demonstrations, primarily led, have been ongoing throughout the summer.

On Sunday, she declared her intention to remain the MP for Brighton Pavilion, aiming to increase her focus on active politics. Elected in 2008 as the Green Party's first sole leader for England and Wales, after they moved away from having dual principal speakers, she later became their first Member of Parliament in the 2010 general election. Via Twitter, she stated her resignation as leader was to allow a new Green Party leader to emerge. Elaborating on BBC Radio 4's Westminster Hour, she said her decision not to seek re-election as leader was to provide opportunities for others to gain recognition, raise their profile within the party, and hopefully get elected themselves. In her announcement, she highlighted the party's recent successes, including securing their first seat in Westminster, gaining control of their first local council, and increasing their vote share in the recent election.

Corrie McKeague, a 23-year-old Royal Air Force gunner stationed at RAF Honington in Suffolk, disappeared after a night out in Bury St Edmunds on the morning of September 24. His mother, Nicola Urquhart, stated on the BBC's Victoria Derbyshire program that it was out of the ordinary for him to vanish without a trace. She added that it was typical of Mr. Mckeague to get into a car with someone he didn't know. Mr. Mckeague, originally from Dunfermline, Fife, was last seen on CCTV at 3:20 AM BST walking alone and eating takeaway food in Bury St Edmunds. His mobile phone was tracked from Bury St Edmunds to the Barton Mills area on September 24. Ms. Urquhart noted that the phone data indicated a 28-minute journey, corresponding to the driving time between the two locations. The whereabouts of the phone remain unknown.

Regina Hungerford, a 56-year-old teacher, refuted allegations of striking a 17-year-old student who was listening to music during her class at Merthyr Tydfil College. Despite her denial, a disciplinary panel concluded that physical contact likely occurred, deeming her behavior "unacceptable." The Education Workforce Council suspended her on Thursday, stating that allowing her to teach again was in the "public interest." Mrs. Hungerford admitted to raising her voice and slamming a book on the desk of the "provocative and disruptive" teenager while he was listening to rap music, but consistently denied hitting his head. Although she was acquitted of criminal assault charges against the student during a math lesson for students with learning difficulties, an appeal, a disciplinary panel determined in November that she likely made physical contact with the pupil's head or hand. The panel concluded that her actions were "inappropriate."

Eric Morecambe acquired the Jensen Interceptor in 1968 and stored it at his residence until its sale to an auction house in 2014. Silverstone Auctions, the buyer, commissioned Jensen experts Cropredy Bridge to renovate the engine, brakes, and body. Morecambe, who passed away in 1984, was the only owner of the car, which was manufactured at Jensen's West Bromwich plant on September 23, 1968. Silverstone Auctions, based in Hertfordshire Warwickshire, has created a website detailing the car's history and restoration, featuring insights from Morecambe's chauffeur, Mike Fountain, who occasionally drove Morecambe and his wife Joan. Fountain recalled that due to the car's two-seater design, space was limited, often leaving Morecambe "screwed up in the back". Despite this, Fountain noted that the Jensen was the Lancashire native's preferred vehicle.

Following a Supreme Court decision, N Srinivasan has temporarily stepped aside as head of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). Srinivasan, considered the most influential cricket administrator globally, owns a team in the lucrative Indian Premier League (IPL). Despite his recent election as chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) in February, scheduled to begin in July, former Indian captain Sunil Gavaskar was appointed interim BCCI president last month. The Supreme Court has directed the BCCI to form a panel to investigate corruption allegations against Srinivasan and twelve others, including players, stating they "cannot close our eyes" to the serious nature of the accusations.

The march was led by individuals directly affected by the suicide bombings at Belgium's airport and metro station, which resulted in 32 fatalities. According to Belgian media, the demonstration was "calm and silent." Originally scheduled for the week following the March 22 attacks, the march was delayed at the request of authorities due to security concerns. On Sunday, relatives of the deceased, along with paramedics, airport employees, and people of various faiths, participated in the march, carrying flowers to honor the victims. The procession passed through Molenbeek, the neighborhood where many of the alleged perpetrators of the Brussels and Paris attacks resided, before concluding at the temporary memorial located outside the city's stock exchange. Hassan Bousetta, one of the march's organizers, stated to AFP that "When our fellow citizens, defenceless civilians, are cut down in a cowardly attack, all citizens should stand up to express their disgust and solidarity."

Uefa is considering adopting goal-line technology, but if approved, their current system of having extra assistant referees behind each goal would continue. The matter was debated on Friday, with a final decision expected in January. Goal-line technology has been used in the Premier League since the 2013-14 season and by Fifa at the 2014 World Cup. Uefa general secretary Gianni Infantino stated at a Paris press conference that there was a "positive" outlook regarding its use, despite some "logistical challenges." He added that the topic has been under consideration for a while and that its implementation for Euro 2016 would extend to the Champions League and Europa League the following season, supplementing the existing five assistant referees. While the final decision is set for January, the executive committee seems largely in favor of the change.

The company reported a net profit of A$45.6 million ($32.4 million; £22.7 million), a 56.7% rise compared to the same period last year. Domino's attributed these strong results to "organic growth," asserting that it had overcome the challenges of the current global economic climate. The pizza chain also announced its second profit upgrade since December on Wednesday, causing its stock price to jump by over 10%. Domino's Australia, officially known as Domino's Pizza Enterprises and listed in Sydney, holds the master franchise rights for the Domino's brand in Australia, Belgium, France, Germany, Japan, and the Netherlands. The company noted that its Japanese operations had expanded by 48 stores in the six months leading up to December, while its Australian and New Zealand operations were on schedule to open more than 50 stores.

Carlos Brathwaite's four successive sixes against Ben Stokes in the final over led to a heartbreaking defeat for England against the West Indies. Despite this, Cook praised Stokes as an exceptional talent and cricketer, confident he possesses the resilience to overcome the setback and perform brilliantly in the future, like scoring 250 in a Test match. Cook acknowledged Brathwaite's incredible hitting, noting that while Stokes might want a do-over of his first delivery, his second wasn't far off, yet still traveled a remarkable 94 meters. Expressing his devastation, Cook admitted to BBC Essex that he doesn't usually get emotional watching cricket. He lamented that the otherwise brilliant tournament ended poorly with the final over not going as planned. Cook's county team, Essex, is set to begin a new chapter under their new coach, Chris Silverwood, on Sunday.

Authorities suspect the man overdosed on heroin possibly laced with fentanyl or carfentanyl, both significantly stronger than typical street heroin. Police discovered him unconscious at a residence in Fitzwilliam, near Wakefield, on Sunday, and he subsequently died in a hospital. A 43-year-old male has been apprehended concerning this death. Det Ch Insp Stuart Spencer of West Yorkshire Police is cautioning regular heroin users, especially those buying from street dealers, to exercise extreme caution regarding their drug supply. This warning follows several fatalities in Hull, Barnsley, Leeds, and Normanton, West Yorkshire, attributed to "deadly batches" of heroin. In March, Cleveland Police connected six deaths in Stockton-on-Tees to a specific heroin batch.

Masai Graham's joke, "My dad suggested I register for a donor card, he's a man after my own heart," earned him the top spot. A panel of 10 judges shortlisted the best jokes from the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, and then 2,000 people voted for the winner. Previous winners of the Dave TV channel-sponsored competition include Tim Vine, Stewart Francis, and Zoe Lyon. Graham, a West Bromwich native who was previously shortlisted in 2014 and 2015, expressed his delight, saying, "It's an incredible honour to land Joke of the Fringe. Not bad for someone from West Brom!" Stuart Mitchell came in second with the joke: "Why is it old people say 'there's no place like home', yet when you put them in one..." The judges had to endure an average of 60 different comedy shows.

Erika Murray, 31, was arrested Thursday night after a neighbor, concerned about the welfare of other children in the home, contacted police. Upon investigation, detectives discovered the bodies within the house, which they characterized as squalid and infested with vermin. Ms. Murray entered a not-guilty plea to all charges on Friday, including concealment of fetal death, witness intimidation, and allowing significant harm to a child. Her attorney suggested she may be suffering from mental illness. "People seek explanations in situations like these... but mental illness isn't always a source of clear answers," stated Ms. Murray's lawyer, Keith Halpern, following her court appearance. According to Tim Connolly, a spokesman for the Worcester district attorney, police initially responded to the Blackstone residence after a ten-year-old boy living there approached a neighbor, reportedly asking, "How do you get a baby to stop crying?"

Jack Whitley, Chelsea's goalkeeper from 1907 to 1914, represented The Blues in their inaugural top-flight season. Upon his death, he requested burial in Brompton Cemetery, despite residing outside London at the time. The Chelsea Supporters' Trust has launched a crowdfunding campaign to fund a gravestone for Whitley, as it's thought his widow lacked the means for a marked grave. Chelsea's official historian, Rick Glanvill, emphasized the significance of a headstone for Whitley, stating it would "mean a huge amount". Glanvill had been researching the links between the club and the cemetery, noting its unique proximity to the football ground, and that while the club's first owner and director were buried there, something was still lacking.

The 24-year-old all-rounder Ben Stokes exited the game in Sharjah with his arm supported by a sling, the result of a diving effort to grab a catch. Stokes, positioned at backward square leg, dived attempting to catch Sarfraz Ahmed's shot off Samit Patel's bowling. England's Stuart Broad told BBC Sport, "We knew immediately he was hurt when he landed." Broad added, "It's concerning, but we have sufficient batting and bowling depth to compensate should he be unable to continue." Stokes was visibly in pain as he lay prone, and after medical attention, he left the field with his shirt fashioned into a temporary sling.

In April 2014, Boko Haram abducted 276 girls, later releasing 21 in October following Red Cross negotiations. While in government custody since their release, the girls returned to Chibok for Christmas but were confined to a politician's residence, according to family members who spoke with the BBC. They were not permitted to visit their homes or attend Christmas church services with their families. Though brought to a local assembly member's house to reunite with parents, they were restricted from going home. One distraught father lamented, "I can't believe my daughter is so near, yet can't come home," criticizing the situation as akin to another imprisonment, preventing even Christmas Day church attendance. Another parent reported a soldier confiscating his phone when he attempted to photograph his daughter, stating, "I snapped a picture of myself and my daughter but the security guys came."

Police identified Banjong Pongphon, the mayor of Padang Besar, as a "key suspect" who "wielded great influence" in the region. Padang Besar, a sub-district in southern Songkhla province, is where 26 bodies were recovered from mass graves last week. According to the UN refugee agency, 25,000 migrants from Myanmar and Bangladesh boarded smugglers' boats in the first quarter of 2015, doubling the number from the same period in 2014. The UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) reported that smugglers' camps in the forests and plantations around Padang Besar are primary destinations for these migrants. The cause of death for those exhumed from the graves in Songkhla remains undetermined.

The police federation, representing 1,000 county officers, has launched a public awareness campaign, including bus and newspaper advertisements, cautioning that traditional policing methods are at risk due to funding cuts. They highlight that Wiltshire Police has lost 153 officers since 2010. While Chief Constable Mike Veale acknowledges the impact of these cuts, he maintains the force's dedication to local policing. The federation's "Cuts Have Consequences" campaign asserts that Wiltshire already has the fewest officers per capita in the UK. They warn that with a 16% workforce reduction, response times are suffering, leaving communities vulnerable at night, and allowing drink-drivers to evade justice. The federation points out that the force has already cut £17 million from its budget and faces at least another £10 million in cuts. Federation chairman Mike White explained that staffing and wages comprise 80% of the policing budget.

To honor Edgar Mobbs, a former England international and Northampton Saints captain, a charity match mirroring the England vs. Scotland game he organized on January 30, 1915, is set for January 24, 2015, at Olney Rugby Club. Mobbs's original match aimed to enlist athletes into his World War One battalion. The commemorative event will feature players from the East Midlands facing The 1st Battalion of the Yorkshire Regiment, and a game between Olney Ladies and the Army Women's XV. Edgar Mobbs, born in Northampton in 1882, began his career in Olney and captained Northampton Rugby Football Club from 1907. Earning seven England caps after his 1909 debut try against Australia, he rose from private to battalion commander, fighting in major battles and receiving the Distinguished Service Order and two mentions in Despatches before his death on July 31, during the battle of Passchendale.

A charity report reveals that over half of the world's 21 million refugees are being hosted by ten countries that collectively represent only 2.5% of the global GDP. Amnesty International's secretary general, Salil Shetty, urged wealthier countries to significantly increase their refugee intake, citing the UK as a "sad example" of shirking responsibility. UN figures show the UK has accepted approximately 8,000 Syrian refugees since 2011, while the US has taken in just 12,000. Recent data from the UN refugee agency indicates that China, Russia, and Gulf states have resettled no Syrian refugees. In contrast, Jordan, with a GDP 1.2% the size of the UK's, hosts nearly 655,000 Syrian refugees, and with over 2.7 million refugees in total, it shelters more than any other nation. Turkey has taken in over 2.5 million people, Pakistan 1.6 million, and Lebanon over 1.5 million.

On Monday afternoon, a CCTV camera recorded an incident outside Jonathan Gwyer's Whitstable residence, showing a man emptying the contents of his food waste bin into the adjacent general waste bin after inspecting it. Serco, the waste management company, has issued an apology for the "completely unacceptable" actions of one of its agency employees. Gwyer, a resident of Colombia Avenue, expressed his shock and disappointment, feeling his recycling efforts were futile, and questioning the purpose of separating waste. While acknowledging the ease of using a single bin for all waste, he primarily held Serco accountable, rather than the individual worker, recognizing the challenging nature of the job. He noted a recent increase in rushed and chaotic behavior among the workers. Serco affirmed their commitment to recycling in an official statement.

The Community Charge Debt bill sets a deadline to prevent local councils from chasing unpaid poll tax debts. The Scottish independence referendum resulted in more people registering to vote, and these expanded electoral rolls were then used to locate individuals with outstanding debts. The Scottish government has pledged to compensate local authorities for this. The poll tax, also known as the community charge, was abolished in Scotland in 1993, after being in effect for only four years. Introduced by Margaret Thatcher's Conservative government in Scotland in 1989, ahead of the rest of the UK, this unpopular tax, which replaced the existing rates system, triggered widespread public demonstrations. The total amount of poll tax arrears recovered by Scottish local authorities has decreased in recent years, falling to below £350,000 in 2013-14, with some councils stopping debt recovery altogether. Deputy First Minister John Swinney described the poll tax as a "hated levy" that inflicted hardship on Scottish communities and was widely condemned as an unworkable and universally opposed tax.

Libya has been in turmoil since Muammar Gaddafi's removal in 2011. Fayez Sarraj, the leader of the UN-supported government, has been meeting with his rival Khalifa Haftar in the United Arab Emirates this week. Haftar, who leads the Libyan National Army (LNA) and holds power in the east, has resisted international attempts to resolve the Libyan conflict, refusing to recognize Sarraj's UN-backed Government of National Accord (GNA) since its formation in 2015. According to Reuters, a source close to the GNA leadership stated that the two parties initially tried to negotiate a joint statement on Wednesday before deciding to issue separate ones. An IPCC report determined that the rape could have been avoided if arrest forms had been promptly completed. Detective Superintendent Rachel Walker stated that officers attended misconduct meetings. The Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC) found that PC Sofi Essex should be held accountable for misconduct because she failed to create the necessary "arrest package"—the paperwork required before an arrest attempt can begin—when requested. The IPCC stated that the delay in completing the paperwork prevented any action from being taken to locate and arrest Craig Hutsby before he committed the rape. The IPCC also concluded that PC Joseph Lovelock should be held accountable for misconduct for improperly completing a form for the victim, which resulted in her not being identified as being at high risk of harm and appropriate measures

The victorious team claimed a $1 million (£650,000) prize, earned by defeating South Korean team Koo Tigers in the Berlin-based final, witnessed by a crowd of 15,000. SKT1 secured the championship with a 3-1 victory, with Koo Tigers being the only team in the entire competition to win a game against them. "We've played Koo many times before and have a good history against them," SKT1's Gyeong-hwan Jang commented after the match. "We observed that Koo hadn't changed much over the last year, and our expectations proved correct." Jang, also known as Marin, was recognized as SKT1's most valuable player for his crucial contribution to the team's second title win, despite only two players remaining from their 2013 victory.

Before his retirement in 2012, 32-year-old Taibu represented Zimbabwe in 28 Test matches and 150 ODIs. Nick Gordon, Hightown's publicity officer, initially suspected a prank when Taibu contacted them, stating, "When he explained who he was I thought it was a hoax." However, after verifying his identity through Zimbabwean cricket contacts, discussions progressed, and Gordon acknowledged, "It's a real coup for us." The former wicketkeeper-batsman is potentially set to debut for the Second Division team against Alder on April 24. Gordon told BBC Radio Merseyside that Taibu reached out after the club posted an advertisement seeking an overseas player for the season. He added, "It's not every day that a club like Hightown St Mary's signs a player like Tatenda," emphasizing the unexpected nature of the signing. "I had to do a double take, it was so unusual."

Despite contrasting political ideologies, President Obama stated that the US and Vietnam are strengthening their collaboration. Experts suggest that the US and Vietnam are pursuing closer relations to counter China's growing assertiveness. This month commemorates the 40th anniversary of the Vietnam War's conclusion. Obama acknowledged the challenging history and ongoing political differences between the two countries but highlighted the development of a constructive relationship built on mutual respect, benefiting both populations. Mr. Trong characterized the discussions as "cordial, constructive, positive, and frank," emphasizing the transformation from former adversaries to friends and comprehensive partners, expressing confidence in the continued growth of their relationship and extending an invitation to Mr. Obama to visit Vietnam.

Al-Shabab previously claimed responsibility for the 2013 Westgate mall attack in Nairobi, which resulted in 67 fatalities. Speaking to CNN, he described the threat as representing "a new phase" of terrorism, characterized by an increase in attacks carried out by "independent actors in their homelands." He emphasized the need to take any terrorist organization's call for attacks on specific locations seriously. However, he clarified that he was not advising the public to avoid the malls mentioned by the militants. The video featured a man with a British accent, his face fully covered, calling on al-Shabab supporters to attack "American or...".

Following discussions with Irish Taoiseach Enda Kenny, the Prime Minister characterized the UK and Ireland as "close friends." Kenny expressed his satisfaction with the evolving relationship between the two nations. Cameron is scheduled to attend a state dinner alongside the Queen and Duke of Edinburgh, who are currently on a four-day visit—the first of its kind by a reigning British monarch since Ireland's independence. Cameron emphasized that the Queen's visit highlights the potential for an even stronger relationship, one rooted in trade, investment, economic ties, and opportunities for neighboring allies. He also noted the Queen's "enormous sensitivity" towards the complex history shared by the UK and Ireland. While Cameron and Kenny previously met in Downing Street in April, this marks their first encounter on Irish soil since Kenny assumed office in March.

Using names of organizations such as NASA and the Environmental Protection Agency, these accounts directly criticize the president, who has dismissed climate change as a hoax. The @RogueNASA account identifies itself as the "unofficial 'Resistance' team of NASA," clarifying that it's not an official NASA account, nor is it managed by government employees, but rather offers facts with a bit of sarcasm. BBC News reached out to @ActualEPAFacts, a rogue Environmental Protection Agency account, which stated its purpose was to ensure the continued sharing of factual information about climate change and other scientific research during the Trump administration. The account claimed to be run by three EPA employees who were motivated to act after a gagging order prevented them from discussing their research in interviews. Media reports have indicated that the Trump administration has attempted to restrict communication with the public from certain government agencies, including the EPA. The official EPA Twitter account has been inactive since January 19, the day before Mr. Trump's inauguration.

The Labour party is supporting the campaign to remain in the EU, and Jeremy Corbyn, who has frequently voiced criticisms of the EU, has been encouraged to take a more prominent role in advocating for it. Members of Parliament cautioned him that the referendum could be "lost" unless the party presented a more "passionate" argument for remaining. According to his spokesperson, he plans to deliver a "big" speech on the EU "in due course." While visiting Dagenham, Corbyn acknowledged that there are aspects of the EU that need to be challenged, but stated that "at the moment we're campaigning because we want this sense of unity across Europe." He explained that Labour is campaigning "on issues of social justice across Europe," highlighting the social chapter, which outlines EU policies on workers' rights, and the Working Time Directive, which regulates employees' working hours. At Preston Crown Court, Matthew Eteson, 42, is contesting a charge of manslaughter by gross negligence in connection with the deaths of Kelly Webster, 36, and Lauren Thornton. The mother and daughter died in their sleep on a boat on Windermere in April 2013. Prosecutor Graham Reeds QC stated that the family's Easter bank holiday trip to the Lake District to celebrate a friend's birthday turned tragic on April 1st when Eteson allegedly moved a generator from the deck and used it to operate a 1kW fan heater inside the sleeping area. The court heard that the carbon monoxide detectors were disabled, providing no warning of the deadly gas buildup. Both victims, from Leyland, Lancashire, were discovered deceased in their beds on the second-hand Bayliner 285 motor cruiser Arniston, with lethal concentrations of carbon monoxide in their systems.

During routine maintenance on Reactor Three, EDF Energy discovered cracks in three graphite bricks. The company stated that the issue, similar to "keyway root cracking" found in the other reactor last year, poses no safety risks and does not affect reactor operation. According to EDF Energy, this information is being released to demonstrate their dedication to openness and transparency. Station director Colin Weir emphasized that nuclear safety is the company's top priority, and they operate with significant safety margins, including those for graphite bricks. He added that the acceptable level of cracking is significantly lower than what would cause any impact.

The company responsible for the London Array wind farm announced a three-year study to assess the potential impact of additional turbines on red-throated divers. Their initial plan involved expanding the wind farm, situated between Kent and Essex, to include 341 turbines. This region serves as the winter habitat for approximately 6,500 red-throated divers, constituting at least a third of the UK's total population. London Array has officially asked The Crown Estate to end the lease agreement for the second phase area and has also cancelled the reserved grid capacity at the National Grid substation in Graveney, Kent. The wind farm project, located 10 miles north of Ramsgate, Kent, received approval in 2006, contingent on the protection of red-throated divers during the phase two expansion, which aimed to add 166 more turbines. Had Mr. McClarty rejoined the UUP, they would have secured two executive seats. His choice leaves them with one, granting Alliance one by default. McClarty stated that numerous constituents had asked him to stay independent, a commitment he wanted to honor. He acknowledged his strong negotiating position, potentially allowing him to secure a ministry, but emphasized that his decision wasn't self-serving. He also expressed reservations about the UUP's organizational structure, describing it as a decentralized collection of associations lacking central oversight. BBC's Gareth Gordon noted that McClarty, who departed the Ulster Unionists in January after being deselected, refuted claims of his decision being motivated by revenge, adding that this development would undoubtedly be a setback for his former party.

Robert Hannigan, the director of GCHQ since 2014, announced his resignation, citing family considerations. He expressed pride in his accomplishments but noted that two decades in public service had significantly impacted his family. Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson acknowledged Hannigan's role in modernizing national security defenses against terrorism during his GCHQ tenure. Prior to leading GCHQ, Hannigan served as director general of defense and intelligence at the Foreign Office. In his resignation letter, he highlighted the lives saved both domestically and internationally due to GCHQ's efforts, but felt it was time for a leadership transition. Hannigan believed a new director should be in place.

According to IHS, the "caliphate" declared by IS two years prior had diminished to 68,300 sq km (26,370 sq miles). This territorial reduction has prompted IS to escalate attacks targeting civilians in both the Middle East and Europe, with a likely continuation of this trend, the report stated. The previous week witnessed nearly 300 fatalities in Baghdad due to an IS suicide bombing, occurring shortly after the Iraqi government announced the complete recapture of Falluja, located just west of Baghdad. IHS noted that in January 2015, half a year after IS's declaration of a caliphate, the group held approximately 90,800 sq km of Iraqi and Syrian land. At Cardiff Crown Court, David Poole admitted to entrapping Adnan Khalid, 27, who was facing charges of grooming a 14-year-old. Poole, 38, stood accused of providing misleading testimony during Khalid's trial, which involved the defendant from Porth, Rhondda Cynon Taff. Judge Thomas Crowther QC ultimately delivered a formal not guilty verdict and rebuked the paedophile hunting group, H Division, founded by Poole, for causing the trial to collapse. Poole, from Hereford, had created a fictitious profile named Chloe on Plenty of Fish, posing as a 14-year-old, and subsequently arranged a meeting with Khalid in Cardiff after communicating via WhatsApp, secretly filming the encounter. Khalid, who denied the charges, claimed he believed he was communicating with a woman over 18. Poole's late arrival to court, followed by a false claim of handing over photographic evidence to the police, led to Judge Crowther's criticism.

The 29-year-old Jamie Vardy rescheduled his wedding twice, once last year and again from June, to participate in Euro 2016. England's coach, Roy Hodgson, acknowledged Vardy's need for a break to get married. Vardy, who secured England's 2-1 victory against Turkey with a goal on Sunday, confirmed that he would have Wednesday off, but would resume training afterward. Hodgson reassured that Vardy's position on the team was secure, while also mentioning the need to assess other players. Vardy, who contributed 24 Premier League goals to Leicester's title win, began the match against Turkey at Etihad Stadium on the left side of the attacking trio, later shifting to the center and scoring the decisive goal after Harry Kane's opener.

NHS England has introduced a walk-in service designed to decrease the number of doctor's appointments and combat the excessive use of antibiotics. This initiative is projected to lower the demand on GPs, potentially saving the NHS millions annually. However, pharmacies express concerns that funding reductions could threaten the program's success. The Sore Throat Test and Treat service, previously tested in 35 Boots pharmacies, distinguishes between viral infections, which are unresponsive to antibiotics, and bacterial infections. A quick throat swab test, analyzing tongue sugars, yields results within five minutes. Patients who would benefit from antibiotics will receive prescriptions directly from the pharmacist, eliminating the need for a GP visit. NHS chief executive Simon Stevens announced that the program will be implemented nationwide in the upcoming year, with Dr. Adam Roberts, a microbiologist specializing in antibiotic resistance at University College London, describing it as "quite an innovative step."

This action followed Russia's announcement of an agreement with "moderate" rebels to reduce conflict in the region. However, analysts express uncertainty about the deal's enforceability. Eastern Ghouta was one of four "de-escalation zones" established in a May agreement between Russia, Iran, and Turkey. According to a Syrian army statement, the cessation of hostilities in Eastern Ghouta began at midday local time on Saturday (09:00 GMT), with a warning that "the army will retaliate in a suitable manner to any violation." Faylaq al-Rahman, a rebel group, welcomed the pause and called on the government to honor it. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported isolated shelling incidents after the ceasefire's implementation but no significant combat. Earlier, Russia announced the signing of an agreement with rebels in Cairo regarding the operational details of the safe zone.

In August, south of Brookmans Park, an A320 pilot reported a near miss with a white quadcopter drone that "flashed past" the aircraft. The UK Airprox Board determined that a collision was narrowly avoided due to chance, as there was insufficient time to react. Air traffic control confirmed that the A320 pilot reported an object passing overhead around 18:45 BST on August 15, 2016, north of Potters Bar. Although air traffic control noted another aircraft had crossed above, the pilot described the object as being under a meter in size, red and white with red and blue stripes on two rotor arms. Regulations mandate that drone operators adhere to Air Navigation Order (ANO) 2016 articles concerning the operation of small unmanned aircraft.

On Tuesday, the hashtag #penuriecarburantdansunfilm, meaning "fuel shortage in a film," dominated Twitter trends in France, surpassing 5,000 tweets. This surge followed a strike impacting all eight of France's oil refineries due to new labor laws. Reports indicate that approximately 20% of the country's petrol stations are either out of fuel or experiencing supply shortages. French social media users referenced movies like Total Recall, a science fiction film with versions from 1990 and 2012, drawing a connection to the French oil and gas giant, Total. Furthermore, some users creatively altered film titles, such as transforming Pulp Fiction into Pump Friction, to mirror the fuel scarcity.

Following the discovery of cheating by 54 student officers, an investigation into the Garverville, east Belfast, college revealed a "pseudo-militaristic" environment characterized by an excessive focus on punishment. The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) has agreed to implement 50 recommended reforms. Chief Constable George Hamilton and other senior PSNI officials are scheduled to meet with the Policing Board to discuss a plan for addressing the identified issues. Several immediate changes have been made to the 22-week training program, including ending the practice of marching students to and from classes and discontinuing military-style "show parades" as a disciplinary measure. Student groups will now be called "classes" instead of "squads." The PSNI's plan outlines 34 changes targeted for completion by the end of March of the following year.

The Royal couple's itinerary commenced with a visit to the Seamus Heaney Homeplace Centre in Bellaghy, where they had the opportunity to interact with the poet's relatives. Their trip includes planned engagements in Londonderry, Belfast, and County Down. While in Bellaghy, they explored the visitor's centre, a place that served as inspiration for many of Heaney's famous verses. Prince Charles, a long-time admirer of the Nobel laureate's work, had previously met Heaney several times. Following their time in Bellaghy, they proceeded to the North West Cancer Centre at Altnagelvin Hospital in Londonderry to engage with staff and patients. Their Tuesday evening concluded with attendance at a musical event held at Hillsborough Castle in County Down.

The single-lane swing bridge spanning the River Weaver Navigation in Northwich dates back to 1908. Local parish councillors, supported by MP George Osborne, are petitioning for improvements, describing rush hour traffic as "mayhem." Cheshire West and Chester Council have announced an upcoming feasibility study. The Winnington Turn Bridge, a Grade II listed structure and early electrically powered swing bridge on the A533 to the M56, experiences significant delays. Barnton Parish Council Chair Dilys Hooper reports typical wait times of 40 minutes during peak hours, characterizing the situation as chaotic and a free-for-all. With plans for at least 4,300 new homes in the Northwich area, Ms. Hooper anticipates further strain on the bridge's capacity.

On Monday evening, a group of eight men disguised as police officers breached the airport fence and boarded a Swiss-bound plane. They stole an estimated $50 million (Â£32 million; 37 million euros) worth of gems from the cargo hold and fled through the same opening. Authorities discovered a burned vehicle near the airport shortly after. According to Antwerp World Diamond Centre's Caroline De Wolf, the stolen gems were worth "a gigantic sum." Initial reports indicated a higher value, with Belgian state broadcaster estimating 350 million euros ($468 million). An unnamed spokeswoman from the Antwerp center described the robbery as "one of the biggest" ever, confirming the diamonds were "rough stones" en route from Antwerp, the world's leading diamond trade center, to Zurich.

In 2010, Cardiff had Wales' largest deficit at £494 million, equivalent to £1,450 per resident, while Merthyr Tydfil had the UK's highest per capita deficit at £2,268. Councils disputed the report's validity, stating they had addressed pension affordability. The Taxpayers Alliance examined 101 local government pension schemes across the UK, using 2010-11 annual statements and actuarial estimates to determine funding. The organization argued that final salary schemes were "inflexible and too expensive," requiring immediate reform, and suggested councils should take action.

Data indicates that the postponement of culling in 2012 incurred a cost of £2.5 million, followed by expenditures of £9.8 million in 2013 and £4.5 million in 2014. Opponents of the cull have described the policy as "disastrous" and an increasingly "unacceptable burden on the taxpayer." The Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) stated that operational costs decreased by half between 2013 and 2014, with farmers covering additional expenses. Bovine TB, a disease transmissible from badgers to cattle, poses a major threat to cattle farming. Regular cattle testing is conducted, and TB-positive animals are culled – in 2014, 26,413 infected cattle were slaughtered in England. However, concerns have arisen regarding the culls' efficacy in controlling TB transmission and the humane treatment of badgers during nighttime shootings. The figures were disclosed by The, following a Freedom of Information Act request.

On May 22nd, 40-year-old Christopher Kelly fatally strangled 51-year-old Dorothy Beattie at her residence in Dunoon, Argyll and Bute. Glasgow's High Court was informed that the assault occurred following an alleged insult by Ms. Beattie concerning Kelly's children. Kelly, who confessed to a general practitioner leading to his arrest, initially faced a murder charge but admitted to the reduced charge of culpable homicide. The court was told that Kelly had previously worked as a support worker for Ms. Beattie, who had several health issues, including seizures. The divorced mother and Kelly developed a friendship and frequently spent time together. However, he attacked her at her home after she purportedly made "derogatory" comments regarding his children. Kelly strangled Ms. Beattie before leaving the premises, only to return later and discover her deceased.

On Thursday, State Prosecutor Marilyn Mosby revealed the amended charges in the Freddie Gray case, retaining the most severe charge of second-degree murder. Gray's death, which occurred a week after sustaining a critical spinal cord injury while in police custody in April, ignited widespread protests, followed by riots and looting in Baltimore. Mosby explained that modifying charges during an active investigation is a common and appropriate practice based on evolving evidence. While the grand jury declined to indict on the false imprisonment charges initially filed by Mosby, who argued Gray's arrest was unlawful, they did introduce new reckless endangerment charges absent from the original announcement three weeks prior. Mosby maintains that Gray's neck was broken during handcuffing and placement in a police van, and that officers disregarded his repeated requests for help.

Baboucarr Ceesay, a 21-year-old from Gambia, is presumed dead after the Libyan fishing vessel he was on capsized in the Mediterranean Sea on Sunday. His aunt, Jessica Sey from Cheltenham, expressed her family's grief, stating they "will never get justice" and emphasized the need for increased migrant risk awareness. She condemned those who exploit migrants, stating they "have got to be held to account." Mrs. Sey stressed that this issue is not just a foreign one, but directly impacts their community. She described her nephew's journey to the UK as "a desperate way out" that ultimately cost him his life. Despite being a talented football player with a comfortable life in Gambia, he desired a better life in Europe and embarked on the perilous journey with a friend, traveling by boat from Banjul to Guinea and then crossing the Sahara.

For the past two seasons, a machine learning algorithm has outperformed BBC football pundit Mark Lawrenson's predictions, prompting its creators to challenge fantasy football enthusiasts to do the same. Researchers suggest the algorithm could also aid players in creating more effective teams. Fantasy football, created in the UK in 1971 by Bernie Donnelly, involves users building virtual teams of real footballers and earning points based on their on-field performance. Initially a small pastime, it has evolved into a thriving online industry with ad-supported versions, downloadable apps, and betting opportunities. In the free Fantasy Premier League salary cap game, fantasy managers can test their skills against Squadguru's AI in the "Challenge the Squadguru" league.

According to one account, the explosion occurred as people were queuing for food. The camp provides refuge for individuals displaced by conflict in the tribal regions bordering Afghanistan, an area known to harbor Taliban and al-Qaeda-affiliated militants. However, police indicate that the camp is also used as a refuge by some of these militants. No organization has claimed responsibility for the attack. Attacks on refugee camps in Pakistan are highly unusual, although concerns have existed for years regarding potential militant infiltration of Jalozai and other camps. The BBC's M Ilyas Khan reports from Islamabad that individuals associated with Lashkar-e-Islam, a militant group, were recently apprehended by a government-supported tribal force. Police suspect that Thursday's bombing may be a retaliatory act. Live television broadcasts depicted ambulances transporting blast victims to hospitals, and the bomb left a crater as police examined the debris.

According to a city council report, the July 2015 yacht races increased tourism and improved the city's image. The report did, however, point out issues like spectator ticketing confusion and unattractive steel fencing. One of the changes for the upcoming event is the removal of evening entertainment. The four-day weekend event in July 2015, organized by TeamOrigin Events, served as the inaugural stage of the sailing series, with Sir Ben Ainslie Racing (BAR) initiating Britain's campaign for the 35th America's Cup. Although Saturday's races drew roughly 100,000 viewers, Sunday's races were called off due to severe weather, leading to the evacuation of public viewing areas. The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge were among those who were let down, and social media users voiced concerns about spectator amenities.

Security forces used tear gas and live ammunition to disperse predominantly Shia Muslim protesters demonstrating against government corruption and inadequate security measures. A curfew was implemented in Baghdad but has since been lifted. This marks the second instance this month of protesters breaching the city's government district. Shia cleric Moqtada Sadr denounced the forceful response and expressed his backing for the demonstrators' "peaceful [and] spontaneous revolt." Reports indicate that at least 50 protesters sustained injuries. The demonstrators claim that the government is failing to implement necessary reforms while simultaneously grappling with its fight against the Islamic State group (IS) and diminishing oil income. The Sunni jihadist group maintains control over areas in western and northern Iraq and has claimed responsibility for a series of recent deadly attacks. Some protesters successfully entered the prime minister's office and parliament building. Baghdad's Green Zone is home to the parliament, important government facilities, and numerous foreign embassies.

In a public statement, Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister Peter O'Neill announced a meeting with Australia's Immigration Minister Peter Dutton in Port Moresby, where both nations concurred on the closure of the Manus Island Regional Processing Centre. This decision follows the PNG Supreme Court's April ruling that the detention of asylum seekers and refugees at the facility was unconstitutional. While the center, currently holding 854 men, will not be shut down immediately, Prime Minister O'Neill indicated that various alternatives are being explored and put into action. He stressed the need for a deliberate and cautious approach that considers the interests of Papua New Guineans and the welfare of the asylum seekers and refugees. It is worth noting that Australia has a policy of transferring asylum seekers arriving by boat to offshore detention facilities.

The BBC Three online platform will provide weekly coverage of the Gfinity Elite Series, where 160 gamers will battle for a £225,000 prize in front of live audiences. While e-sports already has a substantial online viewership, one expert believes the BBC's involvement could draw in new fans. The agreement includes broadcasts of exclusive content from the Gfinity tournament in west London. Gamers will compete in Street Fighter V, Counter Strike: Global Offensive, and Rocket League. Currently, Twitch and YouTube dominate the e-sports streaming landscape, but traditional TV channels like Ginx in the UK are also showing events. Although the BBC has previously aired e-sports highlights, they claim the Gfinity coverage will be "on a much larger scale." IHS analyst Piers Harding-Rolls commented on the development.

This interactive display can mirror a smartphone's touchscreen, a complete computer keyboard, or even piano keys. The laser projector is also capable of projecting images and videos onto walls. The Smart Cast phone was revealed at Lenovo's Tech World conference in Beijing, alongside a new smartwatch. Lenovo stated that the laser projector, measuring a mere 34mm x 26mm x 5mm, eliminates the need for focusing to produce clear images on walls or other flat surfaces. A demonstration video illustrates how rotating the lens mount transforms the device from a typical wall projector into "surface mode," enabling display projection on surfaces.

A Metropolitan Police Federation poll assessing officer sentiment on firearms in light of ongoing terrorism risks revealed that only 6% of the 11,000 respondents felt the number of armed officers was "adequate," despite the Met's plan to add 600. With the UK's international terrorism threat level remaining at "severe" since August 2014, the survey indicated that 43% wanted more specialist firearm officers, and 26% thought all officers should be routinely armed, while 12% would never carry a firearm. The data also showed 2,139 authorized firearms officers (6.7% of total police ranks), 3,974 police firearms operations between March 2015 and March 2016, and 7 incidents involving police firearm discharge in 2015-16. Strong support for Tasers was evident, with 75% advocating for universal access. The poll also explored whether the presence of armed police offers reassurance.

Geraint Thomas, 28, plays a crucial role in Team Sky's efforts to support Chris Froome in his bid for a second consecutive Tour de France victory. Thomas expressed concerns about the treacherous cobblestone sections, especially after Froome underwent an X-ray following a crash on stage four. He noted the potential for rain to abruptly end a rider's race, emphasizing the devastating impact after a year of training. Thomas hopes for dry conditions to prevent accidents. Froome's crash occurred early in the 163.5km stage four, caused by touching wheels within the peloton. Despite suffering a grazed hip and wrist, the 29-year-old quickly resumed the race after medical attention. Following Marcel Kittel's stage win, Froome sits seventh overall, just two seconds behind leader Vincenzo Nibali.

This case involves a Virginia school district's attempt to bar a 17-year-old transgender student, born female, from using the boys' restroom. With a ruling anticipated by the end of June, the Supreme Court faces the possibility of a 4-4 deadlock due to the vacancy left by Antonin Scalia's passing. The central issue has created division among school districts across the country, as they grapple with policies regarding transgender students' bathroom access based on birth certificates. The Supreme Court agreed to hear an appeal from Gloucester County, Virginia, effectively suspending a lower court's mandate that transgender student Gavin Grimm be permitted to use the boys' facilities. Grimm, who identifies as male, initiated legal action against the school board after coming out as transgender in his freshman year.

Angus Campbell, leader of Comhairle nan Eilean Siar, highlighted the disparity in airfares, noting that the airline operating the Stornoway route offered more affordable flights to the Algarve. A Facebook campaign addressing this issue has garnered over 11,000 "likes." Loganair, Flybe's partner for island routes, defended its pricing, citing discounted fares for children, students, hospital visitors, and island residents. Campbell emphasized that reducing airfare costs is a key objective of Our Islands Our Future, an initiative aimed at securing greater autonomy for the councils of Shetland, Orkney, and the Western Isles. He pointed out the high cost of flights, stating that a round-trip flight from Stornoway to Glasgow on Flybe could cost £351, while comparable flights elsewhere were cheaper.

The police force has declined to comment to the BBC. The Police Federation has filed a complaint with the Independent Police Complaints Commission (IPCC). Reportedly, the force invoked the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act (RIPA), intended for crime-related surveillance or public safety concerns, to uncover the source of the information. The Echo claims the application was made after it published a story based on an internal police report detailing institutionalized racism within the force. A Cleveland Police spokeswoman informed the paper that she could "neither confirm nor deny" if a RIPA application had been submitted to monitor the phone activity of three journalists, a police officer, a solicitor, and the then-chairman of the Cleveland Police Federation.
